title: Lower-Data Differential Attack on RECTANGLE-80
summary: A claimed lower-data RECTANGLE-80 attack uses a reportedly better same-round distinguisher but remains unverified; instantiate it and determine its time and memory costs.

formal_statement.body: Open question. For RECTANGLE-80, determine whether a previously claimed lower-data differential attack, based on a distinguisher reported to achieve better probability without reducing round coverage, can be fully specified and verified using the key-guessing techniques presented in Generic Framework for Key-Guessing Improvements. The claimed attack lacks a description and time-complexity analysis and was not verified because of the large time complexity of its key-guessing phase. If the attack can be instantiated, quantify its time and memory complexity and compare these costs with those of the RECTANGLE-80 attack presented in Generic Framework for Key-Guessing Improvements.

scope.domain: Differential cryptanalysis of the RECTANGLE-80 block cipher using key-guessing techniques.
parameters: Data complexity — the claimed attack's intended improvement
Distinguisher probability and round coverage — the reported advantage at unchanged coverage
Time and memory complexity — costs to quantify and compare
scope.unresolved_remainder: Fully specify and verify the claimed attack using the paper's key-guessing techniques, then quantify and compare its time and memory complexity against the paper's RECTANGLE-80 attack.

progress.summary: The source reports a claimed lower-data differential attack but says that no description or time analysis was given and that verification was blocked by the key-guessing phase's large time complexity. It conjectures that the paper's techniques could make the attack work, while expecting worse time and memory costs than its own attack.
citation_labels: Marek Broll et al., Generic Framework for Key-Guessing Improvements
